A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a future linear collider with c m. energy of 0.5 Te V, with polarized beams and an integrated luminosity of 100 fb − 1, can explore a large region of parameter space for the general set (or ‘matrix’) of contact-interaction couplings.
, in the case of a linear collider, the use of model-dependent assumptions is unnecessary and may even be detrimental to the physics reach.
, in the case of e + e − collisions, beam polarization can significantly improve the sensitivity to new physics in contact interaction scenarios.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the reach in the model-independent analysis is comparable to the one obtained with the model-dependent approach, but that in general, the model-independent analysis allows for a better discrimination among the various contact interaction scenarios.

, when the beam polarization is taken into account, the model-independent constraints can be significantly more stringent than those obtained from a model-dependent analysis, and that the model-independent constraints are more stringent than the model-dependent ones for the same number of measurements.

the model-independent approach is more powerful than the model-dependent one in constraining the contact-interaction couplings, and that the reach of the linear collider in this respect is comparable to that of the LHC.
